name: Millrose Properties, Inc.
reason: Land-banking REIT spun out of Lennar in 2025 with only ~2 years of history, 4.3x net debt/EBITDA and heavy single-customer (Lennar) and housing-cycle dependence.

name: FTAI Aviation Ltd.
reason: Recently transformed from lessor to engine aftermarket/module business; EPS at 1.0x 10y max with EBIT margin in 91st pctile and lumpy losses in 6 of 11 years make 10-year forecasting unreliable.

name: Builders FirstSource, Inc.
reason: Housing-cyclical building-materials distributor whose EPS fell from $18.71 (2022) to $6.89 with margin back to 5.2%; acquisition-driven and 3.6x net debt/EBITDA.

name: Axos Financial, Inc.
reason: Strong record (EPS CAGR 16%, 8/10 years >=7%) but a fast-growing internet bank with rate-sensitive, higher-cost deposits and CRE/lender-finance credit exposure, EPS at 10y peak, that cannot be underwritten through a credit cycle with confidence.

name: Power Solutions International, Inc.
reason: EPS at 1.0x 10y max and EBIT margin 15% in 90th pctile vs 3% 10y average on a data-center power boom, with a history of losses and accounting restatements; cyclical peak earnings.

name: Charter Communications, Inc.
reason: Broadband faces a credible fiber and fixed-wireless share threat within 5 years while margin is at a 10y high (24.4%) and net debt/EBITDA is 4.4x; leverage-funded buybacks drove EPS.

name: Albertsons Cos., Inc.
reason: Low-margin (2.1% EBIT) grocer with EPS down 7.6%/yr over 5 years, 3.4x net debt/EBITDA and no specialness; cheap but ordinary.

name: Regions Financial Corp.
reason: Ordinary regional bank whose earnings are set by the rate/credit cycle (EPS 0.94x 10y peak, revenue CAGR 5.7%); a bargain without specialness.

name: Travel + Leisure Co.
reason: Timeshare seller reliant on consumer financing with 6.3x net debt/EBITDA and EPS CAGR of only 2.2% over 10 years.

name: Ameriprise Financial, Inc.
reason: Advice-led wealth franchise with EPS CAGR 15.5% (8/10 years >=7%), negative net debt and steady share shrink; market/rate sensitivity is real but EPS grew even in 2022, so a route to >=7% growth looks plausible.

name: Fidelity National Information Services, Inc.
reason: Mid-transformation (Worldpay exit, Issuer Solutions purchase) with EPS CAGR of 1% over 5 years, a 611% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and 2.9x net debt/EBITDA; core banking moat is real but the forward path is opaque.

name: FB Financial Corp.
reason: Regional bank with mortgage-banking exposure whose EPS grew only 1.4%/yr over 5 years; rate/credit-cycle earnings with no clear specialness.

name: Oaktree Specialty Lending Corp.
reason: BDC whose earnings are set by credit spreads and base rates; EPS at 0.72x 10y max and down 2.4%/yr over 10 years.

name: Global Partners LP
reason: Fuel wholesaler/distributor with ~1% EBIT margins, commodity-driven earnings (EPS swung from $10.02 to $2.11) and 6.2x net debt/EBITDA.

name: GameStop Corp.
reason: Physical game retailer in secular decline (revenue -9%/yr over 10 years); recent EPS driven by interest income on a cash pile, not the core business.

name: United Airlines Holdings, Inc.
reason: Airline earnings set by fuel, capacity and the economic cycle; EPS CAGR -1.1% over 10 years with a -$27.57 loss in 2020.

name: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd.
reason: Cruise operator with 5.6x net debt/EBITDA, EPS still at 0.41x the 2019 level and heavy post-COVID dilution; balance sheet could not comfortably survive a recession.

name: Invesco Ltd.
reason: Market-driven asset manager facing passive fee pressure; EPS down 1.8%/yr over 10 years with margin falling from 27.8% to 19.0%.

name: AT&T, Inc.
reason: Mature telecom with EPS CAGR of 0.4% over 10 years and revenue shrinking 1.5%/yr; no plausible route to >=7% EPS growth.

name: Bright Horizons Family Solutions, Inc.
reason: Employer-sponsored childcare and back-up care leader with sticky corporate clients, EPS CAGR 9.4% (9/10 years >=7% ex-COVID) and margin recovering to 12.3%; net debt/EBITDA of 3.5x and a 73% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap need checking.
